shortDesc: The divine awakening (Bodhon) of Goddess Durga, invocation beneath the Bilva tree, and formal welcoming rites (Adhibas).
guidelines: Devotees observe morning fasting until Kalparambho concludes. Evening is ideal for attending the vibrant Adhibas and Dhak welcoming ceremonies.

events.title: Kalparambho & Bilva Vriksha Puja
events.desc: The sacred ritual vow to conduct Durga Puja, followed by awakening Devi Durga under the auspicious Bilva (Wood-Apple) tree.
events.significance: Marks the awakening of the cosmic Mother after Her celestial slumber.

events.title: Ghat Sthapana & Chokkhudan
events.desc: Placement of the sanctified water pot (Mangal Ghat) and the final traditional brushstroke painting the eyes of Goddess Durga.
events.significance: Imbues the clay murti with divine sight and spiritual consciousness.

events.title: Devi Amontron & Adhibas
events.desc: The formal ceremonial welcome of the Goddess with 27 sacred auspicious items (including turmeric, sacred earth, cowrie, and betel leaves).
events.significance: Sanctifies the deity's presence on earth for the 4-day festival.

events.title: Evening Aarti & Pandal Inauguration
events.desc: First evening Sandhya Aarti with 108 lamps, rhythmic Kanshor-Ghonta, and thunderous celebratory Dhak drum beats as pandals open.
events.significance: Commencement of public pandal hopping and devotional festivities across Kolkata.

shortDesc: The sacred river ablution of Nabapatrika (Kola Bou), life consecration (Pran Pratistha), and grand daytime Bhog feast.
guidelines: Witness the holy sunrise procession of Kola Bou at the Ganges ghats. Wear fresh traditional attire for morning Saptami Anjali.

events.title: Nabapatrika Pravesh & Kola Bou Snan
events.desc: Sacred dawn bathing of the plantain bride (bundled nine sacred agricultural plants) in the holy River Ganges and wrapping in red-bordered white sari.
events.significance: Embodies Goddess Durga as Mother Nature and the nine divine planetary energies.

events.title: Saptami Puja & Pran Pratistha
events.desc: Infusing the idol with life energy through Vedic mantras, followed by Navagraha (nine planets) and Mahisasuramardini worship.
events.significance: The deity becomes fully manifest and receptive to the prayers of devotees.

events.title: Saptami Bhog Nivedan
events.desc: Offering of the grand vegetarian feast: fragrant Gobindobhog Khichuri, Labra mixed vegetables, Beguni, Chanar Dalna, Payesh, and Chutney.
events.significance: Consecrated food distributed to thousands of devotees as Mahaprasad.

events.title: Sandhya Aarti & Dhunuchi Dance
events.desc: Evening lamp adoration accompanied by traditional Dhunuchi dance holding smoldering clay pots with burning camphor and frankincense.
events.significance: Purifies the surroundings and creates an atmosphere of spiritual ecstasy.

shortDesc: The pinnacle of Durga Puja: morning Pushpanjali, divine Kumari Puja, and the sacred 48-minute Sandhi Puja with 108 lamps and lotuses.
guidelines: Strict fasting observed by devotees until completing morning Mahashtami Pushpanjali. Sandhi Puja is the most sacred time for prayer.

events.title: Maha Ashtami Vrata & Shodashopachara
events.desc: 16 sacred royal offerings presented to Goddess Durga, including silk garments, sandalwood, jewelry, and fragrant flowers.
events.significance: Supreme devotional adoration of Goddess Durga as the cosmic protector.

events.title: Mahashtami Pushpanjali
events.desc: Devotees gather in crisp new sarees and kurtas, holding red hibiscus flowers and bel leaves to chant the universal Pushpanjali stotram.
events.significance: Direct personal prayer seeking divine blessings, peace, and health.

events.title: Kumari Puja (Worship of the Living Goddess)
events.desc: Worship of a young virgin girl as the living incarnation of Goddess Durga's unblemished purity and cosmic feminine energy.
events.significance: Pioneered by Swami Vivekananda at Belur Math to honor the divinity inherent in every woman.

events.title: Sandhi Puja (108 Lotus & 108 Lamps)
events.desc: The supreme 48-minute sacred juncture between Ashtami and Navami. 108 earthen lamps are lit, and 108 red lotus flowers are offered.
events.significance: Commemorates the exact moment Devi Durga assumed the ferocious Chamunda avatar to vanquish the demons Chanda and Munda.

shortDesc: Celebration of victory over Mahishasura, the grand Maha Yajna (sacred fire offering), rich Navami Bhog, and all-night Dhunuchi Naach.
guidelines: Participate in the sacred havan and offer bel leaves into the holy fire. Ideal night for all-night pandal hopping sprints.

events.title: Maha Navami Snan & Devi Puja
events.desc: Morning sacred bath and ritual adoration of Devi Chamunda following Her victory over Mahishasura.
events.significance: Celebrates the triumph of righteousness and inner virtue over darkness.

events.title: Maha Navami Yajna (Sacred Fire Havan)
events.desc: Vedic fire sacrifice with pure cow ghee, sacred wood, bel leaves, and symbolic vegetable sacrifices (pumpkin/sugarcane).
events.significance: Cleanses cosmic negative energies and radiates peace and universal welfare.

events.title: Navami Maha Bhog Feast
events.desc: Grand culinary feast featuring fragrant Ghee Polao, Kosha Mangsho (or Shahi Chanar Dalna), Chutney, and hot Mishti.
events.significance: Festive community feasting celebrating divine abundance.

events.title: Grand Dhunuchi Naach Championship
events.desc: Hypnotic, ecstatic dance performances balancing smoking clay pots on teeth, palms, and foreheads to thumping dhak beats.
events.significance: Ultimate expression of festive energy, joy, and Bengali cultural pride.

shortDesc: Emotional farewell to Maa Durga, vibrant Sindoor Khela vermilion celebrations, sacred river immersion (Bisarjan), and Shubho Bijoya.
guidelines: Women participate in Devi Boron with betel leaves and sweets. Touch the feet of elders for Shubho Bijoya blessings and share homemade sweets.

events.title: Dashami Puja & Darpan Bisarjan
events.desc: The final ritual worship where the Goddess's reflection is symbolically immersed in a brass mirror (Darpan) filled with holy Ganga water.
events.significance: Symbolizes that the Goddess now resides in the hearts of Her devotees.

events.title: Devi Boron & Sindoor Khela
events.desc: Married women wipe the Goddess's face with betel leaves, feed Her sweets, and playfully smear bright red vermilion on Her forehead and each other.
events.significance: Celebrates womanhood, longevity, marital happiness, and feminine solidarity.

events.title: Bisarjan & Ghat Parikrama
events.desc: The grand immersion procession to the Ganges ghats with thunderous cries of 'Aschhe bochhor abar hobe!' (Mother will return next year!).
events.significance: Devi Durga returns to Her heavenly abode on Mount Kailash.

events.title: Shubho Bijoya & Mishti Mukh
events.desc: Embracing (Kola-kuli), touching elders' feet for blessings, and sharing handmade Nimki, Narkol Naru, Ghugni, and Rosogolla.
events.significance: Spreads universal forgiveness, brotherhood, and sweetness across society.
